To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the optimal placement for side groups is at least a third along the bridge, (ii) the optimal number of side groups is the minimum necessary to achieve the desired degree of superscaling, and (iii) once a side group has been properly placed, additional groups do not enhance the nonlinear response.

the optimum position for side groups on conjugated structures is a third of the distance along the bridge from the end, that additional side groups do nothing, and that the optimum position is independent of the length of the bridge.

(1) the best response for intrinsic nonlinear optical response is obtained when side groups are attached to conjugated structures at a distance of 1/3 to 2/3 along the bridge; (2) the best response is independent of the number of side groups; (3) the best response scales as the square root of the number of atoms in the conjugated structure; and (4) the best response occurs in structures with a large number of atoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of quasi-one-dimensional quantum structures for nonlinear optical applications.
the development of new, high-performance materials for nonlinear optics, and our approach to this problem is the optimization of the geometry of conjugated systems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the optimization of superscaling, the most important design parameter is the placement of side groups.
the design of conjugated structures is not a matter of trial and error, but rather a matter of following a simple set of design rules.
the best superscaling quasi-one- dimensional structures are the ones with a short side group attached a third of the length of the bridge from the center.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a properly designed conjugated structure should be a long, thin, straight bridge with a side group placed a third of the distance from its end.
the response of conjugated structures is not enhanced by attaching side groups to their ends, and that the response is optimized by placing a single side group a third of the length along the bridge.
the best way to design a conjugated molecule for intrinsic nonlinear response is to attach short side groups along the bridge, but not at the end.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the topology of the system is important, the geometry of the system is more important in determining the response of the molecule.
the response of a conjugated structure can be enhanced significantly by a judicious choice of side groups.
the intrinsic response of a conjugated system is determined by the shape of the structure and is not a simple additive property.
